result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both have visible labels, a native date picker, full-width tap targets and no extra fields. B is a bit more finished: its controls are larger, and its short helper text ('We'll send you a copy of your waiver', 'Takes about a minute') explains what to expect without turning into marketing. A's hint says 'Day, month and year', but the field shows mm/dd/yyyy, so the hint contradicts the format. The screenshots show only the starting state, so I couldn't check error messages, focus handling, the in-progress state or the success state, and scored those items conservatively for both. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both screenshots show only the initial state. They both have visible labels, a native date picker, a large checkbox row inside a bordered box and a full-width button, so I couldn't check error messages, focus handling, loading or success states, or the 360px layout. A is slightly ahead: it has bigger touch targets, a short intro, and a note under the email field saying a copy of the waiver will be sent, which tells people what happens next. B is clean and correct but plainer, and keeps the generic 'Submit' button text.
